L8·N9373unmasked layer
This neuron has weak, diffuse positive firing on mid-sentence continuation tokens (function words like "a"/"to" and the final noun of a list/phrase, e.g. "videos", "services", "idea"), and is most strongly (negatively) driven by segment-initial tokens — sentence/paragraph starts after a newline, greetings, and capitalized name fragments — so it primarily encodes "inside a phrase" vs. "start of a new segment."

This neuron is essentially always negative and non-selective: it sits at its most negative (i.e., "fires" per the shown 7–10 annotations) uniformly across ordinary fluent English prose — especially commas, conjunctions/function words ("and", "with", "so") and the `<|begin_of_text|>` token in list-like descriptive text — and drifts toward zero only on rare/odd sub-word fragments in noisy or garbled text ("ina", "ers", " Tall", stray "(" in citation lists), so it reads as a generic "normal running text" tonic signal rather than a semantic detector.
